validity.researcher_notes: The row's ONLY citation, and the harvested wiki-citation pool's ONLY entry, is one document: petro-mag.org's digital flipbook of 'Petroleum Magazine' (مجلة البترول), the Egyptian Ministry of Petroleum's own house magazine, Volume 61 / December 2024 edition (petromagazine@petroleum.gov.eg). This is a JS flipbook viewer -- the HTML shell carries no extractable article text, every page is a JPG image -- so url_verifier's automated 'contains expected value' check is structurally blind here: its PASS on Length/Diameter and FAIL on Status in the worklist are both coincidental (the numbers 23/26 it matched are just page numbers in the issue's own table-of-contents list of pages 1-146, not the pipeline's specs). I did not trust that automated check either way and instead pulled the actual page images and read them directly (fetched via the same id path: /Uploads/Images/d48e45eb-.../.jpg, page ordering recovered from each thumbnail's alt-text). Page 138 is the 'Petroleum Pipelines Co. (PPC)' company profile spread ('انابيب البترول .. التوسع فى مشروعات البنية الاساسية'), and the following page (site-internal label '139A') carries PPC's own itemized list of '11 EIA approvals obtained from the Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency' for new pipeline projects. Item 5 on that list reads verbatim: 'انشاء خط خام مسطرد / الهايكستب قطر 26" بطول 23 كم من مستودعات مسطرد وحتى مجمع بلوف الهايكستب' = 'Construction of a Musturad/Al-Haykastab crude oil line, 26in diameter, 23km length, from Musturad depots to the Haykastab valve/block complex.' That is an EXACT match to GEM's Length=23km, Diameter=26in, StartLocation=Musturad (Al-Qalyubia), EndLocation=Huckstep (Cairo), Fuel=Oil (خط خام = crude line), and is a first-party primary source (PPC describing its own project) published in the ministry's own magazine -- about as strong single-source sourcing as exists in this dataset. Classification as PipelineType=transmission is reasonable (a trunk line between two depot/valve complexes, not a gathering or process line), consistent with how sibling depot-to-depot crude lines in this roster (P7330, P7977/P7978) are classified. The one real caveat: this item sits in an 'EIA approvals obtained' list, which documents environmental clearance, not confirmed construction start -- so 'construction' status is an inference (EIA-approved = actively moving forward) rather than a literal statement that groundbreaking has occurred. That inference is applied uniformly across every sibling row drawn from this same EIA list (P7315, P7319, P7325, P7326, P7328, P7331 all read 'construction' off the identical list), so it is a pre-existing tracker-wide convention, not a defect specific to this row -- flagging it here as context, not as a fix. I could not find a second, fully independent source (outside this WebSearch-quota-exhausted session) that separately names this exact 23km/26in Musturad-Huckstep segment; per the confidence rubric this stays single-source/medium, not high, until someone re-runs a search pass.

validity.researcher_notes: P7914's Owner1 is staged as 'General Petroleum Co' at 100%, cited to the same petro-mag.org PPC-profile page used for every other field. That is very likely a mix-up between two distinct, real Egyptian entities: (1) 'General Petroleum Company' (GPC), an EGPC upstream exploration & production joint-operating company that produces oil in the Gulf of Suez / Ras Gharib area, and has no documented role in pipeline construction; and (2) 'Petroleum Pipelines Company' (PPC, شركة أنابيب البترول), the actual company that WROTE the source article -- its own letterhead/logo on the page ('شركة أنابيب البترول / Petroleum Pipelines Co.', www.ppc.com.eg) identifies it as Egypt's national oil-pipeline builder/operator, and the article's own text states this and the other 10 EIA-approved lines are PPC projects operating under EGPC. This is corroborated three ways: (a) the source page itself, whose masthead names PPC not GPC; (b) GEM's own wiki page for this same pipeline (built from the identical petro-mag.org citation) lists Operator = 'Petroleum Pipeline Company (PPC)' and Owner = 'Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation (EGPC)' -- i.e. even the same-source derivation elsewhere in GEM's own system did not produce 'General Petroleum Co'; and (c) internal roster consistency -- every other pipeline in this 46-row Egypt-oil scope sourced to a PPC/EGPC-style reference (all 15+ rows drawn from this identical petro-mag.org article or its sibling EGPC pages, e.g. P7315/P7319/P7325/P7326/P7328/P7330/P7331/P7332/P7333/P7334/P7335/P7336/P7339/P7340/P7341-P7343) carries Owner1='Egyptian General Petroleum Corp' or 'Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation (EGPC)' -- P7914 is the ONLY row in the entire scope with 'General Petroleum Co' instead. I additionally confirmed via Arabic Wikipedia's dedicated article on the company ('أنابيب البترول (شركة)') that Petroleum Pipelines Co. is a real, independently-documented, separate entity from General Petroleum Co: founded 9 Oct 1962 under Republic Decree-Law 74/1968, operating Egypt's oil-products pipeline network since 1955 (starting with the Suez/Musturad 12in x 134km line) -- an entity distinct in charter and function from an upstream E&P joint-operating company. This is a data-entry attribution error on this one row, not a genuine ownership dispute.

That coincidence is worth recording, but I do not think it is the same physical pipe under two names: the named endpoints do not overlap (Badr vs. Huckstep at the far end; both share only 'Musturad' as a common node, consistent with two DIFFERENT segments radiating from the same Musturad depot hub rather than one line double-counted), the two rows carry different statuses (operating vs construction), and P7330 traces to a generic EGPC reference rather than to this same petro-mag.org EIA-approvals list (which names this project as new/incremental, i.e. does not reference a pre-existing Badr-Musturad line as part of the same build). Read as two separate, similarly-sized radial spurs off the Musturad depot complex, not a duplicate.
